newsitem.title: GERMANY: DASA awaits developments on Thomson-CSF.
newsitem.headline: DASA awaits developments on Thomson-CSF.

text.p: Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA) said on Wednesday it was awaiting developments in the planned private placement of French defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF announced in Paris on Tuesday.

A spokesman said DASA would wait for the French government to shortlist potential buyers before considering joining any talks on joining a new defence grouping which Paris would like to forge around Thomson-CSF.
"Only then will we be able to see more concretely where DASA could be brought in," DASA spokesman Andreas Breitsprecher told Reuters.
Last week, DASA chief executive Manfred Bischoff said the outcome of the Thomson-CSF privatisation was of crucial importance to the European defence industry.
Lossmaking DASA, a unit of auto group Daimler-Benz AG, is keen for Europe to press ahead with the kind of industry consolidation which has already progressed much further in North America.
"We are talking with our main partners over how the European defence industry can be restructured," Breitsprecher added.
The French government said on Tuesday that terms for the private placement of Thomson-CSF would be submitted to the independent Privatisation Commission.
Paris is relaunching the privatisation of Thomson-CSF, part of the Thomson SA group, after having cancelled its previous plan to sell the whole group in one block in December.
The government had previously expressed a preference for a bid by Lagardere for the Thomson group but the Privatisation Commission objected to the terms of the sale.
